lines: An eight channel splitter and merger: a polyphonic cable is split out to eight mono jacks, eight mono jacks are merged into a polyphonic cable, and a knob per channel crossfades between the two
Crossfades one channel of the POLY output between the IN jack of that number and the channel of the POLY input of that number, the IN jack alone fully anticlockwise
A signal merged into the POLY output on the channel matching its number, and the knob for that channel crossfades it against the POLY input
The polyphonic cable that is split out, its channel 1 going to OUT 1, its channel 2 to OUT 2 and so on
Carries the channel of the POLY input matching its number as a mono signal, with no knob acting on it
The eight IN jacks merged into one polyphonic cable, each channel crossfaded against the POLY input by its own knob; the highest numbered IN jack in use sets the channel count
Note — SMExpL immediately to the left adds IN 9 to IN 16, and SMExpR immediately to the right adds OUT 9 to OUT 16
An expander adding eight more merge inputs to SMMix, numbered IN 9 to IN 16; it goes immediately to the left of SMMix
A signal merged into the POLY output of SMMix at the channel matching its number; it arrives there at one tenth of the voltage patched in, and no crossfade knob acts on it
Note — nothing happens unless SMMix is the module immediately to the right; the ACTIVE lamp is lit while it is, and dark while it is not
SMExpL.notes: No source is published for MM_Tools; everything here was read out of the installed 2.0.0 binary. SMExpL multiplies each of its input voltages by 0.1 before handing them to SMMix, while SMMix's own IN 1 to IN 8 are merged unscaled. Nothing on the panel or in the README says so, and it looks like an oversight rather than a design, but it is what the code does: IN 9 to IN 16 land on the POLY output 20dB down.

lines: An expander adding eight more split outputs to SMMix, numbered OUT 9 to OUT 16; it goes immediately to the right of SMMix
Carries the channel of the SMMix POLY input matching its number, 9 through 16, as a mono signal
Note — nothing happens unless SMMix is the module immediately to the left; the ACTIVE lamp is lit while it is, and dark while it is not
Eight sample and hold rows on one panel, sharing a clock, each row with its own trigger input, chance of firing, clock divider, voltage limits and a switch onto a polyphonic output
Sets the rate of the built-in clock, 30 to 900 BPM, which is the common trigger while Common TRG has no cable in it
A rising edge through 0V here is the common trigger, and it replaces the built-in clock; it samples every row that has no cable in its own Trigger input
Carries 10V while the common trigger is high and 0V while it is low, whether that trigger comes from the built-in clock or from Common TRG
Sets the percentage chance that a trigger on that row takes a new sample; a trigger that does not pass leaves the held voltage where it was
Takes a new sample on that row only once every so many triggers, 1 to 64, and the count runs on every trigger the row receives
Sets the lowest voltage that row can hold, -10V to 0V: the bottom of the random range while the row's Signal input is empty, and a floor the sampled voltage is clipped to while it is not
Sets the highest voltage that row can hold, 0V to 10V: the top of the random range while the row's Signal input is empty, and a ceiling the sampled voltage is clipped to while it is not
Puts the voltage that row is holding onto the POLY OUT jack
Packs the rows switched to poly into consecutive channels of POLY OUT; off, each of those rows keeps the channel number matching its own position on the panel
The voltage that row samples; with nothing patched here the row draws a random voltage between its own Range- and Range+ settings instead
A rising edge through 0V takes a sample on that row; with nothing patched here the row is sampled by the common trigger
The voltage that row is holding, until its next sample replaces it
Carries the held voltage of each row whose To poly switch is on, one channel per row
Note — sLewd immediately to the right adds a slew limiter to the held voltage of every row
SHEight.notes: Ranges read from the installed 2.0.0 binary: Clock 30 to 900 BPM (default 120), Probability 0 to 100% (default 100), Divide by 1 to 64 (default 1), Neg. Range -10V to 0V (default -5V), Pos. Range 0V to 10V (default 5V). Two quirks a person should settle. First, the probability roll is rand() modulo 101 and passes when the setting is strictly greater than the roll, so 100% still misses about one trigger in 101. Second, TRG Out is given the same channel count as POLY OUT, and each row that samples writes 10V onto its own channel of TRG Out without anything setting it back to 0V; only channel 1, which follows the common trigger, is rewritten every sample. The entry describes channel 1 only.

lines: A slew limiter that smooths the eight held voltages of SHEight, one row for each; it goes immediately to the right of SHEight
Sets the curve of that row's slew: a steady rate at one end of its travel, and at the other a rate that falls away as the output nears the new voltage
Sets how fast that row's output climbs to a higher voltage: 1ms per 10V fully anticlockwise, 10ms at the default, 100 seconds fully clockwise, measured with Shape at zero
Sets how fast that row's output falls to a lower voltage: 1ms per 10V fully anticlockwise, 10ms at the default, 100 seconds fully clockwise, measured with Shape at zero
The slewed voltage of that row of SHEight; the slew for the row runs only while a cable is in this jack
Note — nothing happens unless SHEight is the module immediately to the left; the ACTIVE lamp is lit while it is, and dark while it is not
Note — a row is slewed only while a cable is in that row's output jack, so the knobs for a row with an empty jack change nothing
Spreads the channels of a polyphonic cable evenly across a stereo pair, panning each channel at constant power
Sets how wide the channels are spread: at 100% channel 1 is hard left, the last channel hard right and the rest evenly spaced between them; at 0% every channel is centred
Scales both outputs, silent at 0% and unity at 100%; the taper is steep, 50% passing an eighth of the input
The polyphonic cable to be spread, its channel count setting how many positions the spread is divided into
Added to the channel of IN L with the same number before the spread, both then halved; nothing patched here is panned on its own, despite the panel printing IN R
The left side of the spread, polyphonic with one channel per input channel, unless Merge Poly Output sums them onto a single channel
The right side of the spread, polyphonic with one channel per input channel, unless Merge Poly Output sums them onto a single channel
Menu — Merge Poly Output — sums the spread channels down to one channel on each output, making OUT L and OUT R a monophonic stereo pair; it is off until it is switched on
ASSprdr.notes: The panel prints IN L and IN R, but the code gives IN R no pan position of its own: each of its channels is added to the channel of IN L with the same number, the sum is halved, and the pair is then panned to the position that channel of IN L would have had. The pan positions come from a table of evenly spaced values from -1 to +1 for each channel count from 1 to 16, scaled by SPREAD about the centre and applied as a constant power pan over a quarter turn. The volume taper is v divided by (7 minus 6v).

lines: A polyphonic DC blocker, taking the steady offset out of a signal at a corner frequency you set
Sets the filter coefficient, 0.9 to 1: the corner drops as the value rises, around 700Hz at 0.9 and around 35Hz at the default 0.995 on a 44.1kHz sample rate, and it moves with the sample rate
The signal to be filtered, all of its channels
The filtered signal, carrying as many channels as the input
TheCBlocker.notes: The filter is y = x - x1 + k*y1 with k the ADJ. knob, 0.9 to 1, default 0.995, and no sample rate compensation, so the corner given in the line is for 44.1kHz and rises with the rate.

lines: A polyphonic saturator shaped after a valve stage, driving the signal into a soft curve and scaling the result back
Sets how hard the signal is driven into the curve, 1 to 10; the output is scaled back as the drive rises, so a 5V peak stays near 5V and the waveform rounds off instead of growing louder
The signal to be saturated
The saturated signal, carrying as many channels as the input
Tuube.notes: The panel prints DRIVE where the maker's tooltip name is Distortion; they are the same knob, 1 to 10, default 1. The curve is 5 * atan(in * drive / 5) * 4/pi, divided by (2 - 1/drive) as makeup, so a 5V peak comes out at 5V with the drive at 1 and at about 4.93V with it at 10.
